subject: Emerald Systems — SI Technical Ramp & Joint-Lab Scheduling

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@emeraldsys.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emerald Systems — SI Technical Ramp & Joint-Lab Scheduling

Hi Ethan,

Great to meet on the call yesterday — thanks for the time. As discussed, we'd like to run a focused joint-lab with your SI team to accelerate configuration, validate performance at your expected workload, and deliver an initial runbook the consultants can follow when they onboard customer projects.

Proposed objectives (2-day lab):
- Validate model serving throughput for your target QPS and sequence lengths
- Walk through VPC/private deployment checklist and SSO/KMS integration
- Run a short prompt-eval and quality smoke-test that mirrors your production prompts
- Deliver an SI playbook + checklist and lab recording

Prerequisites from Emerald:
- 2 engineers (one infra, one ML) + 1 PM to attend
- Sandbox credentials / a small sample dataset (anonymized) for inference load tests
- SSO admin user or test account for SAML flow testing
I attached a draft workbook and agenda (Emerald_Systems_SI_Workbook.pdf, JointLab_Agenda_v1.odt).

Can you confirm:
1) Desired week (we have open slots Jun 6–10 and Jun 20–24)
2) Names/emails of the SI consultants who will attend
3) Any procurement / legal gating items (NDA status, procurement contact)

If those windows work I'll lock in resources on our end and send a final agenda.

Thanks,

David Kim
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
Email: david.kim@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: Emerald_Systems_SI_Workbook.pdf (PDF stub), JointLab_Agenda_v1.odt (ODT stub)

Thanks David — this looks good. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- SSO: we prefer SAML test flow; I can provide a dev IdP account (Maya will provide details).
- Data: we'll provide a 2GB anonymized sample dataset via a shared S3 bucket; is that sufficient?
- Attendance: tentative: Joel Park (infra), Lina Chen (ML), and myself (product). We'll confirm names by Friday.
- Procurement/NDA: procurement@emeraldsys.com is CC'd — we have a standard mutual NDA already signed (copy attached separately).

Two other asks: 1) can you include a short section in the workbook about model quantization tradeoffs for latency-sensitive workloads, and 2) is a single Redwood SE enough for both days or should we plan two?

Team — forwarding Emerald's reply and initial asks. Quick internal sync so we can commit resources and final agenda. Key points:
- Two-day joint lab for SI enablement; Emerald will send dev IdP and anonymized sample S3 data.
- They requested content on quantization tradeoffs and want to know if one SE is sufficient.
- Tentative attendance: Joel Park (infra), Lina Chen (ML), Ethan.

Proposed assignment:
- Priyom: lead the hands-on lab and run the perf benchmarks; own the lab runbook and templates.
- Laura: create the short quantization + tradeoffs appendix for the workbook and a 15-min slide deck.
- Camila: own stakeholder comms, procurement touchpoints, and capture success criteria for the deal team.

Timing: they asked for Jun 6–10 or Jun 20–24 windows. I'd like to push for Jun 6–7 (earlier momentum) if we have capacity.

Can everyone confirm availability and any constraints by EOD? I'll then send the proposed dates and attach the updated agenda.

Thanks — David

[Forwarded attachment: Emerald_Systems_SI_Workbook.pdf, JointLab_Agenda_v1.odt]

Thanks — availability check: I can cover stakeholder comms and be backup for the runbook capture on Jun 6–7.

Notes / plan:
- Priyom: primary lab lead (agree) — can you confirm you have access to the perf harness (Benchmark v2) and the load generator?
- Laura: quantify appendix: target 10–12 slides + one-page appendix in the workbook; include simple before/after latency numbers for float32 vs 4-bit quant profiles.
- SE coverage: one SE on Day 1 + on-call SE for Day 2 should be sufficient; Priyom may need an extra pair for the perf run if we push higher QPS. I'll request a second SE as contingency.
- Legal/procurement: David, can you confirm the NDA is added to the hubspot record and link procurement contact to the Drive folder?

Deliverables timeline (internal):
- Wed 5/30 EOD: final attendee list and confirmed dates
- Thu 5/31: updated workbook + quantization appendix (Laura)
- Mon 6/3: full runbook + environment access checklist (Priyom + David)

I'll block the tentative Jun 6–7 slot and keep the contingency week of Jun 20–24 idle until we confirm.

—Camila

Ethan / Maya / procurement — thanks for the quick response and for confirming the NDA is on file. We're locking in Jun 6–7 for the joint lab. Below is the finalized agenda and a short prep checklist; attachments: updated workbook (Emerald_Systems_SI_Workbook.pdf v2) and agenda (JointLab_Agenda_v2.odt).

Final agenda (high level):
Day 1 (Jun 6) — Setup & Baseline
- 9:00–9:30 Introductions + success criteria
- 9:30–12:00 VPC/Networking, SAML SSO test, KMS integration walkthrough
- 12:00–13:00 Lunch
- 13:00–17:00 Deploy model variants, run baseline perf tests, record logs

Day 2 (Jun 7) — Optimization & Handoff
- 9:00–10:30 Quantization tradeoffs & latency benchmarking (Laura)
- 10:30–13:00 SI runbook hands-on (Priyom)
- 13:00–14:00 Smoke-test evaluation and acceptance criteria
- 14:00–16:00 Recording + next steps + access handoff

Prep checklist (what we need from Emerald before Jun 3):
- SAML dev IdP details (Maya)
- S3 bucket link with anonymized sample (Joel / Lina)
- Confirm attendee names and email addresses

SE coverage: we'll have one primary SE (David) on-site/virtual for Day 1 and Priyom as the lab lead across both days; Camila will manage stakeholder comms. We have requested a backup SE as contingency.

Next actions:
- Maya / Ethan: confirm IdP and S3 access by Fri 6/1 EOD
- Procurement: confirm any PO/ticketing needs (copied)
- Camila / Priyom / Laura: final deliverables uploaded to the Drive folder by Mon 6/3

Looking forward — I'll send calendar invites once we have attendee names.

Best,
